script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only. Through two games both defenses allow about 4.0 YPC (SF 3.95, ARI 3.98) and 4 passes of 20-plus, so the pack does not show a blowout. SF is the more explosive offense (Evans 103 rec yds, Kittle 92, Robinson 84; Purdy 0.98 EPA vs blitz) while ARI runs through McBride (23 targets, 136 yards) with Allgeier 22 carries and Love 20, and an ARI QB at -0.31 EPA vs blitz. Base: competitive, SF slightly more efficient, both backfields stay split, ARI passing shortens when SF blitzes at 28%.
script.flip1: SF gets up and kills the clock. Black (21 carries, 90 yards) and CMC (20/91) both see rush volume; ARI abandons the run so Allgeier (22/71) and Love (20/70) rush lines die and McBride/Wilson targets rise into the blitz.
script.flip2: ARI controls the ball with the committee and it becomes a slog, or SF is the team trailing. Evans (95 air) and Kittle (88 air) never get the dropbacks to clear their lines, and Black, who is not in the target list, loses carries.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, or inactives in the pack, so nobody can be named as a confirmed next man up. On usage alone ARI is already a committee (Allgeier 22 carries/71 yards, Love 20/70) with Harrison at only 4 targets and 33 yards, and SF already splits carries Black 21/90 and CMC 20/91. Those are current roles, not verified injuries. Late-scratch re-check is impossible from this pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location only: SF allows left 6.89 YPA (19 att), middle 5.75 (8 att), right 7.83 (24 att). ARI allows left 6.71 (14 att), middle 9.53 (15 att), right 8.62 (24 att).
matchup.pressure: SF blitz rate 28%. ARI QB EPA/dropback is -0.31 vs blitz (n=15) and +0.13 with no blitz, so pressure should cut ARI deep yards and push checkdowns. ARI blitzes only 21%, and Purdy is +0.98 EPA vs blitz (n=18) vs +0.38 unblitzed, so ARI pressure does not suppress SF.
matchup.bleeds: SF bleeds the right side (7.83 YPA), not the middle (5.75 on only 8 throws). Run defense is not a bleed: 3.95 YPC and 3 runs of 10-plus; 4 passes of 20-plus on 55 attempts. ARI bleeds the middle (9.53 YPA) and the right (8.62), with 6 runs of 10-plus at 3.98 YPC and 4 explosives on 57 attempts.
matchup.overlap: ARI's primary is McBride (23 targets, 125 air, 136 yards, short-intermediate), but SF's middle is their best area (5.75 YPA), so he does not attack the right-side bleed. Wilson (14 targets, 133 air, only 74 yards) is the deep shot and runs into the blitz, not a coverage hole. Kittle (9 targets, 88 air, 92 yards) and Evans (10 targets, 95 air, 103 yards) do overlap ARI's soft middle and right, but their lines (47.5 and 55.5) sit on recent per-game output (46 and 51.5), so the overlap is real and the price is not.

form: Only weeks 1-2, totals labeled L3, no game splits. ARI: McBride 23/136/125 is the offense; Wilson 14/74/133 is air without conversion; Bourne 11/86/50 is YAC-heavy (86 rec on 50 air); Harrison 4/33/74 is not a weekly yardage role; Allgeier 22/71 (3.23 YPC) and Love 20/70 (3.5 YPC) split the carries; Brissett 4/24 rushing. SF: Black 21/90 (4.29 YPC) matches CMC 20/91 rushing, and CMC adds 12/63/8 receiving; Samuel 11/79/36 and not listed as a rusher; Evans 10/103/95; Kittle 9/92/88; Purdy 8/59 rushing. A single long play could be inside any of these combined totals.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Wilson has turned 133 air yards into only 74 receiving yards, about 37 a game, and SF blitzes 28% into an ARI quarterback at -0.31 EPA versus pressure, so 46.5 sits above both his production and the environment that kills deep shots.
edge_players.must_be_true: He stays the vertical option near 7 targets rather than an 8-target safety valve, SF pressure shows up, and he does not connect on multiple 20-yard shots in a defense that has allowed only 4 of those on 55 attempts.
edge_players.kills_it: ARI falls behind and the deep shots finally hit, especially to the right where SF allows 7.83 YPA, or the two-game total hides one quiet game and his real role is already near 46.5.

edge_players.edge_sentence: CMC has 91 rush yards plus 63 receiving yards, about 77 a game, while Black has taken 21 carries to his 20, so 100.5 combined needs a workload this split has not produced.
edge_players.must_be_true: The Black/CMC split stays near 10 carries each, CMC receiving stays near 6 targets and 31 yards, and this is not a clock-killing SF lead that hands him 15-plus carries.
edge_players.kills_it: SF leads and runs through CMC, or his target-leader role (12 targets) becomes a 50-yard receiving day on ARI's 9.53 middle YPA and the combined line is gone.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so this is not a model check and no 70%+ probability is being trusted. Pack form agrees with both leans: Wilson about 37 per game versus 46.5, and the posted under is the juiced side (-118 versus over -113). CMC about 77 per game versus 100.5; the posted price is essentially even (under -113, over -115.5), which is not a real disagreement and is not a confirmed misprice. Two-game samples only. Bourne over 23.5 (43 per game) and Harrison under 33.5 (16.5 per game) were dropped: the posted lines disagree hard with two-game totals and the counter-case (one spike, or a star role the market still prices) is stronger than the read.

market_rung_price: michaelwilson recyds under 46.5 at -118; christianmccaffrey rushrecyds under 100.5 at -113. No alt rungs in the pack. Nan-priced props (McBride 69, Love rush lines, Allgeier rush 34, Samuel rec 41) were not used because they cannot be priced. One market per player. No passing yards, TDs, or receptions.
pre_mortem: Monday both lost because the missing spread was a SF lead the two-game sample did not show. Wilson cleared 46.5 when ARI trailed, the 28% blitz did not wreck the downfield throws, and one or two of his 9.5-air targets hit a defense that already allowed 4 gains of 20-plus and 7.83 YPA to the right — 74 yards on 133 air was small-sample miss rate, not a role. CMC cleared 100.5 because the Black split (21 carries to 20) was a two-game mirage, clock-killing carries pushed him past 57.5 rushing, and the target-leader role added a receiving spike on ARI's 9.53 middle. That counter-case is why both are leans, not strong.
slip_story: One competitive-game story only, since spread and total were not saved and both defenses have allowed about 4 YPC and 4 explosives. Pressure keeps ARI's deep game under (Wilson recyds under 46.5) and the SF carry split keeps CMC combined under 100.5. Do not add Black rush over 32.5 or SF WR overs; those need a SF-lead or shootout flip. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player. Read only — do not place a bet.
